dedupe_keys.name: chicago energy benchmarking covered buildings list

description: The list of buildings that must comply with the Chicago Energy Benchmarking Ordinance, published by the City of Chicago Sustainability Program on the Chicago Data Portal. Since 2016 it has covered all commercial, institutional and residential buildings larger than 50,000 square feet; owners use it to check whether a property must report by the annual June 1 deadline and to find the six-digit benchmarking ID. The ordinance asks these buildings to track whole-building energy use, report yearly and verify data every three years, and the city says covered buildings are under 1% of Chicago's buildings but about 20% of building energy use. Fields: building ID, address, zip, cohort by sector and size, verification year, community area, ward, latitude and longitude, and census tract. Coverage: the city of Chicago, current list, updated as needed; the portal shows the data last updated on 14 March 2025 and first published on 18 December 2020. Access: open download or API through the Socrata portal. Licence: the portal says see terms of use; cost is free. Caveats: the list gives no energy figures, which sit in the separate energy benchmarking dataset. Useful as an asset inventory of the largest buildings for urban energy planning and adaptation studies, and to link with reported energy use; related records are not yet linked.
